# Feature Specification

## Metadata
- Feature: `eval-oauth-login`
- Profile: `Simple`
- Status: `Approved`
- Owner: eval-harness

## Problem Statement
- Who is affected, what fails, and why now: Users cannot sign in with an existing identity provider, so every session requires a local password.

## Outcome
- Observable result: A user can complete Google OAuth2 login and land on the authenticated home page.
- Minimum useful release: Google OAuth2 only.

## Scope
- In scope: Google OAuth2 authorization code flow for web login.
- Out of scope / non-goals: social profile sync, multi-provider federation.
- Preserved behavior: existing local password login remains available.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `AC-001`: Given an unauthenticated user, When they complete Google OAuth2, Then they receive an authenticated session.
- `AC-002`: Given a cancelled OAuth2 consent, When they return to the app, Then they remain unauthenticated and see a non-blocking error.

## Constraints and Risk
- Constraints: do not store provider refresh tokens in cookies.
- Dependencies/touchpoints: identity provider callback route.
- Risks and mitigations: callback CSRF via state parameter.
- Open questions (blocking only): none.
